concept.name: Risk-on risk-off trading
concept.definition: A macro positioning framework that rotates between higher-risk assets (equities, cyclicals, commodities, credit) in optimistic risk-on regimes and safe havens (Treasuries, gold, cash, reserve currencies) in fearful risk-off regimes, driven by shifts in aggregate investor risk tolerance. The correlated cross-asset moves in these regimes are the phenomenon the framework trades.
concept.intuition: In RORO markets the global portfolio breathes as one organism: when fear rises, everything risky is sold together and everything safe is bought together, so the trade is the regime, not the asset.
concept.mechanics: Define regime indicators (equity momentum, credit spreads, volatility indexes, dollar strength) and shift allocations or take paired positions - long equities against short Treasuries in risk-on, the reverse in risk-off. Dedicated products such as RORO ETFs mechanize the rotation between high-risk equities and low-risk Treasuries.
concept.failure_modes: Regime labels are obvious only in hindsight; choppy transitions whipsaw rotation signals, and structural shifts - such as stock-bond correlation turning positive in inflation regimes - break the canonical risk-on/risk-off pairings.
concept.misconceptions: That risk-off means all risky assets fall and all havens rise every day; RORO describes correlation tendencies in aggregate risk appetite, not a daily law, and idiosyncratic news routinely overrides it.
concept.example: When weak data and falling earnings guidance flip the indicators risk-off, a rotation fund shifts from 80% equities / 20% Treasuries to 30% / 70%, cutting drawdown if the selloff continues but forfeiting the rebound if it does not.
